artworks.title: Juno and Argus
artworks.description: Rubens's Wallraf–Richartz canvas shows Juno claiming the eyes of the slain hundred-eyed watchman — Argus's gaze transferred to the peacock's tail.

artworks.title: Mercury and Argus
artworks.description: Velázquez's Prado night-piece: Mercury pipes Argus to sleep before the killing stroke — the all-seeing guardian undone by music and a single blade.

artworks.title: Mercury and Argus
artworks.description: Rubens's Dresden painting catches Hermes lulling the many-eyed Argus as Io the heifer waits nearby — the spy of Hera about to lose every waking eye.

popCulture.title: Argus Panoptes
popCulture.description: English still calls a watchful guardian argus-eyed — the hundred-eyed giant who never slept, until Hermes closed every lid.

popCulture.title: Peacock
popCulture.description: Hera set Argus' eyes in the peacock's tail — the all-seeing watchman as the bird's spotted plumage.
